review_status: DRAFT - every regulatory note and evidence entry must be checked against Peraturan BPOM No. 23 Tahun 2019 (and its annexes) and the cited literature, and preferably reviewed by a pharmacist or dermatologist, before release. Set 'verified' to true only after that check.
disclaimer: Glowrithm supports your choice of skincare ingredients. It does not diagnose skin diseases and is not a substitute for advice from a dermatologist.

dry.description: Low moisture: skin can look dull or rough, feel tight and show fine, flaky lines.
dry.care_focus: Restore hydration and support the skin barrier.

normal.description: Balanced moisture and oil, even texture and small, barely visible pores.
normal.care_focus: Keep the balance and protect against UV and pollution.

oily.description: High sebum output: visible shine, especially on the T-zone, with enlarged pores.
oily.care_focus: Control excess sebum and keep pores clear without stripping the barrier.

cleanse.title: Cleanse
cleanse.goal: Remove dirt and excess oil without damaging the barrier.

treat.title: Treat
treat.goal: Target the main need of your skin type.

protect.title: Protect
protect.goal: Seal in moisture and defend against UV damage.

oily.headline: Recommended for oily skin
oily.summary: These ingredients help regulate sebum and keep pores clear while respecting your skin barrier.

avoid.name: Heavy occlusives (thick butters, petrolatum-rich creams)
avoid.reason: Feel greasy and can worsen clogged pores on oily skin.

avoid.name: Harsh, high-alcohol toners
avoid.reason: Over-stripping irritates the skin and can trigger rebound oiliness.

dry.headline: Recommended for dry skin
dry.summary: These ingredients draw water into the skin and rebuild the lipid barrier that keeps it there.

avoid.name: Strong foaming surfactants (e.g. sodium lauryl sulfate)
avoid.reason: Strip barrier lipids and increase dryness and tightness.

avoid.name: Fragrance and high denatured-alcohol content
avoid.reason: Common irritants for a weakened skin barrier.

normal.headline: Recommended for normal skin
normal.summary: These ingredients maintain your skin's balance and protect it from free radicals and UV light.

avoid.name: Over-exfoliation (daily strong acids or scrubs)
avoid.reason: Can disrupt a balanced barrier and cause sensitivity.

salicylic_acid.name: Salicylic Acid
salicylic_acid.function: Oil-soluble exfoliant that clears clogged pores
salicylic_acid.how_to_use: Use as a wash-off cleanser once a day; start every other day if your skin is sensitive.

regulatory.note: Restricted cosmetic ingredient: a maximum concentration applies (commonly 2% in leave-on face products under the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive annexes adopted by BPOM) and it is not for children under 3.
regulatory.reference: Peraturan BPOM No. 23 Tahun 2019 - annex of restricted ingredients

salicylic_acid.caution: Can dry or irritate the skin; do not combine with other strong exfoliants.
evidence: CD-3 reference [14]: salicylic acid gel and sebum/acne outcomes

niacinamide.name: Niacinamide
niacinamide.function: Balances sebum and strengthens the skin barrier
benefits: Supports barrier function and evens skin tone
niacinamide.how_to_use: Apply a serum or moisturiser once or twice a day; 2-5% is generally well tolerated.

regulatory.note: Permitted cosmetic ingredient with no specific concentration limit.

niacinamide.caution: Rarely causes flushing at high concentrations.
evidence: CD-3 reference [13]: niacinamide serum randomised controlled trial

zinc_pca.name: Zinc PCA
zinc_pca.function: Soothes blemish-prone skin and helps reduce shine
zinc_pca.how_to_use: Look for it in a lightweight moisturiser or toner used daily.

regulatory.note: Water-soluble zinc salts are restricted to a maximum zinc content (commonly 1% calculated as zinc) under the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive annexes.
regulatory.reference: Peraturan BPOM No. 23 Tahun 2019 - annex of restricted ingredients

evidence: Citation needed: add a clinical reference for zinc PCA before release

sunscreen.name: Broad-spectrum sunscreen
sunscreen.inci: UV filters (e.g. zinc oxide, titanium dioxide)
sunscreen.function: Protects against UVA and UVB damage
sunscreen.how_to_use: Apply generously every morning as the last step; reapply every 2-3 hours outdoors. Oily skin: choose a gel or fluid texture.

regulatory.note: Only UV filters on BPOM's permitted list may be used, each up to its maximum concentration.
regulatory.reference: Peraturan BPOM No. 23 Tahun 2019 - annex of permitted UV filters

evidence: General dermatology guidance: add a sunscreen reference before release

hyaluronic_acid.name: Hyaluronic Acid
hyaluronic_acid.function: Humectant that draws water into the skin
hyaluronic_acid.how_to_use: Apply to slightly damp skin, then seal with a moisturiser.

regulatory.note: Permitted cosmetic ingredient with no specific concentration limit.

ceramide.name: Ceramides
ceramide.function: Repairs and reinforces the skin barrier
benefits: Reduces water loss through the skin
ceramide.how_to_use: Use a ceramide moisturiser morning and night.

regulatory.note: Permitted cosmetic ingredient with no specific concentration limit.

evidence: CD-3 references [11] and [12]: moisturizers and pseudo-ceramide efficacy

glycerin.name: Glycerin
glycerin.function: Gentle humectant found in non-stripping cleansers
glycerin.how_to_use: Choose a mild, low-foam cleanser that lists glycerin near the top of its ingredients.

regulatory.note: Permitted cosmetic ingredient with no specific concentration limit.

shea_butter.name: Shea Butter
shea_butter.function: Emollient that softens skin and seals in moisture
benefits: Forms a protective film against water loss
shea_butter.how_to_use: Use a cream containing shea butter at night or on very dry areas.

regulatory.note: Permitted cosmetic ingredient with no specific concentration limit.

shea_butter.caution: Can feel heavy on oily or acne-prone skin.

vitamin_c.name: Vitamin C
vitamin_c.function: Antioxidant that defends against free radicals and brightens
benefits: Neutralises free radicals from UV and pollution
Helps fade dullness and uneven tone
vitamin_c.how_to_use: Apply a serum in the morning under sunscreen.

regulatory.note: Permitted cosmetic ingredient with no specific concentration limit.

vitamin_c.caution: Pure L-ascorbic acid can sting; derivatives such as sodium ascorbyl phosphate are gentler.
evidence: Add a reference before release (e.g. a review of vitamin C in dermatology)

prohibited.name: Mercury (merkuri)
prohibited.reason: Prohibited in cosmetics by BPOM; damages the kidneys and nervous system.

prohibited.name: Hydroquinone (hidrokinon)
prohibited.reason: Not allowed in skincare cosmetics; a prescription medicine that often appears in illegal whitening creams.

prohibited.name: Rhodamine B (Merah K10) and Merah K3 dyes

personalization_rules.note: Under 18: prefer a gentle wash-off salicylic acid cleanser and ask a pharmacist or dermatologist before using leave-on exfoliants.
personalization_rules.rationale: Conservative safety rule for adolescent skin (team heuristic - validate with an expert).

personalization_rules.note: Age 25+: antioxidant support plus daily sunscreen helps limit photoaging.
personalization_rules.rationale: Photoaging prevention (team heuristic - add a reference).

personalization_rules.note: Age 40+: skin barrier lipids and hydration tend to decline, so ceramides are prioritised.
personalization_rules.rationale: Age-related decline of stratum corneum hydration and sebum (e.g. Luebberding et al., Int. J. Cosmet. Sci., 2013).

personalization_rules.note: On average men produce more sebum, so oil-balancing niacinamide is slightly prioritised.
personalization_rules.rationale: Sex differences in sebum content (e.g. Luebberding et al., Int. J. Cosmet. Sci., 2013).

personalization_rules.note: After menopause skin lipids and hydration drop more noticeably, so extra hydration is prioritised.
personalization_rules.rationale: Sex- and age-related decline of skin surface lipids (e.g. Luebberding et al., 2013).

general_notes: Patch-test each new product on a small area for 24-48 hours.
Introduce one new active ingredient at a time.
Wear sunscreen every morning, whatever your skin type.
Choose products with a BPOM registration number (check at cekbpom.pom.go.id).
If irritation persists, stop the product and consult a dermatologist or pharmacist.
